findings.issue: The note addresses the operator with a second-person imperative (вы-imperative «не ждите»), so it reads as telling the operator to stop waiting for a reply. Per the context sidecar the actor is the agent: dismissing means the agent stops waiting on this ask. The terminal/phone copy for the same English (tui.asks.dismiss.moot_note, relay.ask.dismiss.moot_note) was corrected for exactly this in its own independent audit and names the agent. Root cause is upstream of the translation: the en context sets `tone: "lowercase fragment, imperative"` for this key while its `note` says the agent stops waiting, so a translator following the tone line lands on an operator-addressed imperative. Coder should also change that tone line (e.g. 'lowercase fragment naming what the agent stops doing') so a re-translation does not regress.
findings.proposed: агент больше не будет ждать ответа

findings.issue: «в беседе» is off-corpus for the ru desktop (0 uses in this sense; «чат» 43, «разговор» 135). It also clashes with the reason title right above it («Ответ дан в чате») and with the terminal/phone note «вы уже ответили в чате».

Masculine «нужен» agrees with an implied «запрос», but the receipt in this namespace uses the impersonal neuter («Убрано — больше не нужно»), as do the terminal/phone surfaces («Больше не нужно»). One act should read one way.

Cross-surface divergence: the terminal/phone heading uses «вопрос» for the ask, the desktop uses «запрос». Kept deliberately: «запрос» matches the desktop's own asks panel and rail on the same screen (ui.chat.composer.secret_ask_open «Открыть запросы», ui.shell.rail.ask.aria «Запросы»). Recorded so the two surfaces can converge in one direction; no catalogue change proposed here.
